_comment: TheFlow taxonomy v2 (v1 plus the news topics and signals, NEWS_INTAKE.md). Two closed axes: topic (what it is about) and signal (what kind of event). The model picks only from these lists; it never invents a label. dedup_window_hours lives on the signal axis (DEDUPLICATION.md): a promo_code is stale in hours, analysis in days, regardless of topic. A source may override with flow.dedup_window_hours. Routing targets are NOT here -- they are deployment-specific and live in routing.json (see routing.sample.json).

steam.description: Steam and game drops, sales, inventory, releases, patches
examples: Free case drop this weekend for CS2 players
Steam Summer Sale starts June 26
New Divine skin added to the market

airdrop.description: Testnets, retrodrops, farming tasks, allocations, snapshots
examples: Complete these 3 testnet tasks before the snapshot
Project X confirms retroactive airdrop for early users
Allocation checker is live, claim opens Thursday

crypto.description: Listings, on-chain specifics, crypto market moves, analysis. Not price shouting, not advertising. Stocks, companies and macro belong to `markets`
examples: Token Y lists on Binance with a USDT pair
On-chain analysis of whale accumulation in $ABC
Exchange Z halts withdrawals after a suspected exploit

tools.description: Free offers, service discounts, non-obvious solutions to technical problems
examples: Service X free tier expanded to 100 GB
How to work around the Y rate limit
50% off annual plan for new accounts this week

health.description: Health and the body: medical research, drugs and trials, nutrition, supplements, fitness, weight, sleep, longevity, mental-health practices
examples: Phase 3 trial: a new drug cuts migraine days by half
Large study links daily walking to lower blood pressure
Regulator approves the first pill for a common sleep disorder

mind.description: Psychology and neuroscience: how people think, decide, feel and behave, including the effect of technology and AI on thinking
examples: Study finds people overestimate how much others notice their mistakes
Heavy use of navigation apps linked to weaker spatial memory

money.description: Money and business stories about people and companies: how people earn, new business models, the creator economy, careers, an unusual success or failure with numbers. Market moves and macro belong to `markets`
examples: How a two-person bakery grew into a 40-store chain in five years
Freelancers report earning more from short courses than from client work

markets.description: Stock markets, companies and macro: a notable company's sharp move either way, results and guidance, bankruptcies, layoffs, leadership changes, probes, central banks, inflation and jobs data. Crypto belongs to `crypto`
examples: Shares of Company X surge 40% after record quarterly results
Retailer Y files for bankruptcy protection
The central bank holds rates and signals two cuts this year

other.description: Does not fit any topic above. Routes to #unsorted

promo_code.description: Contains a code that can be redeemed

freebie.description: Something given away to keep: a game, item or currency that stays yours after claiming, or a steep discount on a purchase. Temporary access is NOT a freebie -- a free weekend, trial, demo or preview period grants nothing permanent and belongs to `event` instead.

analysis.description: A breakdown with data and reasoning that bears on the state of the market: supply, prices, availability of tradeable items. The test is whether it changes what a reader would buy, sell or claim. Citing dates and history is not enough -- a retrospective pegged to a calendar occasion (an anniversary, a year in review) is an opinion unless something about supply or price follows from it. 'No new case for 524 days' is analysis: it says nothing tradeable shipped. 'The game turns three' is not.

event.description: An event with a date: a start, a deadline, an active window. Includes time-boxed free access -- a free weekend, a trial or a preview period -- where the thing is only usable while the window is open.

launch.description: A release, a listing, something new going live

outage.description: A failure or outage: the service is down

opinion.description: An opinion without supporting data, or a piece whose data is incidental -- an occasion or anniversary write-up that cites dates and patches but leaves supply, price and availability exactly where they were.

security.description: Funds or accounts are at risk: platform and exchange hacks, contract exploits and drains, rug pulls, phishing waves, compromised accounts, stolen-funds reports, 'do not interact with X' warnings. Distinct from outage, which is only 'the service is down'

research.description: A new study, trial, survey or dataset and what it found. The finding is the news; a press release about a product is `launch`, a commentary without new data is `opinion`

report.description: A news report of a development that already happened: company results, a share-price move, a deal, a layoff, a ruling, a central-bank decision, a data release. Not a study (`research`), not a forecast or commentary (`opinion`)

giveaway_result.description: Announcement of giveaway or contest winners (Победители, <filter>, Розыгрыш завершен, <filter>). Classified once, routed nowhere

stream.description: A livestream announcement or link (<filter>, twitch.tv). Classified once, routed nowhere
